/whyTourWorks/routeLogicSections/0/items.source_en: Two UNESCO World Natural Heritage sites + intangible heritage in one day

⟦G0⟧ and Manjanggul are World Natural Heritage sites inscribed together in 2007 as 'Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes'. Add the haenyeo diving performance, a 2016 Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, and you see three layers of UNESCO heritage in a single day.
Cave first, beach last — the order is the point

Manjanggul opens at 09:00 and is emptiest in its first hour, so the route goes there directly from pickup — you walk the lava tube before the midday tour-bus wave, while the 11–13°C cool is a refreshment rather than a chill. The day then builds through Seongeup and Seongsan to the haenyeo performance, and closes at Hamdeok Beach in the soft late-afternoon light — the closest stop to Jeju City, which keeps the final transfer the shortest of the day.
The real Manjanggul — the original UNESCO lava tube, no longer a substitute
In the past we substituted Micheon Cave during closures, but now you explore Manjanggul itself — one of the world's largest lava tubes, home to the world's largest lava column at 7.6 m high.
All admissions included — the value at this price
⟦G0⟧ ₩5,000 + Manjanggul ₩4,000 (Seongeup free, haenyeo diving performance free) — two World Natural Heritage sites are covered by just ₩9,000 in admissions.

The roughly 30-minute round-trip climb to the crater rim is steep and not right for everyone. There is also a coastal loop path with a similar view and no stairs, so you can choose according to your fitness.

/whyTourWorks/routeLogicSections/0/title.source_en: Why this route is built this way

/routeShapeIntro/subtitle.source_en: An East Jeju loop that runs the island's two UNESCO World Natural Heritage sites in a single day — entering the ⟦G1⟧ right after opening, ahead of the crowds, and completing the same 2007 inscription at ⟦G2⟧ in the afternoon. Between them sits the Joseon-era ⟦G0⟧; after them, the haenyeo diving performance (a UNESCO intangible heritage) and a golden-hour finish at Hamdeok Beach, the closest stop to Jeju City.

/staticQuestions/0/answer.source_en: Yes. Watching the haenyeo diving performance held in the sea near ⟦G0⟧ is part of the route (usually in the afternoon, free). It can be canceled depending on sea and weather conditions, and if canceled we substitute the indoor Haenyeo Museum in Hado-ri to guarantee the haenyeo heritage experience.

/staticQuestions/0/question.source_en: Can I actually watch a haenyeo diving performance?

/staticQuestions/1/answer.source_en: Yes. There is a coastal loop path that offers a similar photo angle without stairs. The crater climb (about 0.8 km round trip, about 30 min) is optional, so you can decide according to your fitness.

/staticQuestions/1/question.source_en: Can I skip the ⟦G0⟧ crater climb?

/staticQuestions/2/answer.source_en: It is a tour by the same operator. The southern tour includes a Hallasan oreum, ⟦G3⟧, ⟦G2⟧, the columnar joints, and the Osulloc tea fields. The eastern tour focuses on ⟦G1⟧, ⟦G0⟧, Manjanggul, and the haenyeo diving performance.

/staticQuestions/2/question.source_en: What is the difference from the southern Jeju UNESCO tour?

/staticQuestions/3/answer.source_en: Manjanggul is a UNESCO World Natural Heritage lava tube included in the route. However, on days it is closed for maintenance or weather (heavy rain, etc.), we substitute a nearby cave such as Micheon Cave at Ilchul Land, part of the same lava-tube system, to keep the cave experience.

/staticQuestions/3/question.source_en: What happens on days when Manjanggul is closed?

/staticQuestions/4/answer.source_en: It is not included. Lunch is separate (about ₩15,000), and the guide will recommend a good local spot.
